# vet402

> Independent verification of the x402 agent-payment economy. vet402 buys what x402 endpoints actually sell, verifies fulfillment against the seller's own declaration, and publishes the results with evidence. It also scores payee wallets on Base, so an x402 API provider or a spending agent can check a counterparty before a payment settles.

x402 settles payments finally and irreversibly, and proof of payment exists on-chain — but proof of delivery does not exist anywhere. Registries can be written for cents and directory metrics can be manufactured, so vet402 does not take either at face value: it measures, states which level of verification a result came from, and says "unverified" when it has not measured. Nothing on the site is presented as an estimate.

Formerly named "Vouch"; renamed to vet402 in August 2026. The production URL is `vet402.com`. The GitHub repository is `kzmttkc/vet402` (the older `kzmttkc/agent-trust` URL still redirects there; cite the new one). Issued API keys and webhook headers keep the `vouch_` / `Vouch-` prefixes for backward compatibility — the old name appearing there is deliberate, not stale documentation.

## Verification levels

Every word used below is defined in one sentence each at https://vet402.com/observatory/methodology#vocabulary, and the same definitions are published as `DefinedTermSet` structured data on that page and in https://vet402.com/llms-full.txt.

This is the published methodology. A result is labelled by the level that produced it and never moves up a level: an L0 probe cannot report settlement, and an L3 opinion is never folded into an L0–L2 fact. L0, L1 and L2 verdicts ship live in the observatory (see "Implemented and live" below): L0 and L1 are full measurements; L2 is a deliberately minimal structural check — parses the response as JSON and confirms the seller's own declared required keys are present, nothing deeper — described exactly as such on https://vet402.com/observatory/methodology. L3 is not built and no opinion is published anywhere on the site.

- **L0 Liveness** — does the endpoint answer correctly? Probe, no purchase. Output: pass / fail / unverified.
- **L1 Settle-through** — does payment settle and a response arrive? Real purchase. Output: n of m settled, n delivered, latency. settled = the transfer re-read on-chain; delivered = settled AND the paid request answered 2xx.
- **L2 Conformance** — does the response match the seller's own declaration? Purchase plus machine diff. Output: match / mismatch / no_declaration / not_checked.
- **L3 Quality** — is the content any good? Published rubric. Output: opinion, and never mixed into an L0–L2 fact.

What the API returns today is a different, older thing: a 0–100 trust or payee score banded ALLOW / WARN / BLOCK. It predates the levels and stays available to API and SDK callers during the transition; observatory verdicts replace it as they ship, and a score is never reported as an L0–L2 result. The front page states this relationship in §2.1. Scoring is fail-closed: an input that could not be read is never reported as an input that was checked and found fine. Such a verdict is marked `degraded`, is not cached, and returns BLOCK to callers, while the public profile pages say "Not verifiable right now" instead of publishing a number.

## Primary

- https://vet402.com/ — the memo: problem, verification levels, what is live, what is still being built
- https://vet402.com/observatory — the L0 register: every catalog-listed x402 endpoint, probed daily against its own declared method, pass / fail / unverified with timestamped evidence
- https://vet402.com/observatory/state — aggregate rates for the whole observed catalog, broken out by chain
- https://vet402.com/observatory/methodology — full definitions for L0 Liveness, L1 Settle-through and L2 Conformance: what each level measures, what it cannot measure, and the publication gate that keeps one bad sample from branding an endpoint dead
- https://vet402.com/docs/api — API reference, including copy-paste curl commands that need no key
- https://vet402.com/accuracy — public accuracy ledger: past verdicts, outcomes, and misfire rate
- https://vet402.com/leaderboard — register of recently verified subjects, ranked
- https://vet402.com/payee — verify a payee, or look one up
- https://vet402.com/corrections — every correction issued to a published result, and what does not count as one
- https://vet402.com/operator-log — public, append-only record of every global operator override (network-wide blacklist), with the address, stated reason, and date; customer-private lists never appear here
- https://vet402.com/faq — x402, ERC-8004, and how scoring works
- https://vet402.com/signup — get an API key (free tier: 1,000 lookups / month)
- https://vet402.com/blog — notes on agent-to-agent payments, x402, and verification
- https://vet402.com/blog/rss.xml — the same posts as RSS
- https://vet402.com/llms-full.txt — full FAQ and blog text, generated from the same modules the HTML uses
- https://vet402.com/openapi.yaml — OpenAPI 3.1 of every public endpoint

Public per-subject pages: `https://vet402.com/payee/{address}`, `https://vet402.com/agent/{agentId}`, and `https://vet402.com/observatory/e/{id}` (one endpoint's full L0/L1/L2 history).

## API — no key required

These are open paths, rate-limited per IP. Nothing below needs an account. Every response carries `RateLimit-Limit`, the ceiling for that path. `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` are per-caller, so they are sent only on responses a shared cache does not replay to someone else — chiefly the `429`, which also carries `Retry-After`. A cached `200` deliberately omits them rather than handing you a counter that belongs to whoever populated the cache. A path under `/api/` that matches no route answers `404` as JSON (`{"error":"not_found","path":...}`), never as an HTML page.

- `GET /api/v1/accuracy` — the accuracy ledger as JSON. `slo.l1_probe_error_rate_pct` is the share of all L1 attempts in the last 7 days whose purchase run did not complete inside vet402 (`request_error` / `in_flight`, counts in `slo.l1_7d`); it is not the held share of the ledger export (`slo.l1_7d.held` of `slo.l1_7d.signed`) and not the "vet402's side" column of /sellers, which classifies each listed Base listing by its latest attempt of any date. Aggregate counts, and the same numbers /accuracy renders **with the same caveats attached**: the `interpretation` object carries the notes that qualify each rate — that a benchmark "detection" counts BLOCK *or* WARN and how many known-bad addresses stopped at WARN, that a 0% false-positive rate means "none were blocked" rather than "all were passed" and how many known-good addresses only reached WARN, and that a rate below the minimum sample is `null` rather than a number. Reading the JSON alone is enough; you are not being asked to parse the HTML to learn what a figure means
- `GET /api/v1/payees/verify?wallet={address}&name={name}` — returns the exact message a payee must sign. Read-only, writes nothing. The message opens with `vet402.com — verified payee registration` and carries a `domain: vet402.com` line, so a signer can tell in the wallet's own signing view which site is asking; it also states the 10-minute validity and that the signature moves no funds. Fetch it rather than constructing it — signatures over the pre-2026-09-05 wording stopped verifying on 2026-09-21
- `POST /api/v1/payees/verify` — publish a verified-payee page and badge by posting that signed message. Free, signature required
- `GET /api/v1/agents/verify` / `POST /api/v1/agents/verify` — the same claim flow for an ERC-8004 agent identity
- `GET /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/passport` — machine-readable agent passport
- `GET /api/badge/{address}.svg` — SVG badge for a payee wallet (states only whether a signed claim exists; carries no score, because a cached score on a third-party page would outlive its freshness window)
- `GET /api/badge/agent/{agentId}.svg` — the same badge for an agent
- `GET /api/badge/endpoint/{id}.svg` — receipt badge for one x402 endpoint, stating its measured settlement (paid attempts settled / paid attempts), facts only
- `GET /api/transparency/operator-overrides` — the machine-readable twin of /operator-log: every global operator blacklist act with address, action, reason, and date; customer-private lists never appear
- `GET /api/demo/score` — one fixed, publicly registered agent, scored live. Returns `live: false` rather than a stale or invented number when it cannot compute one, and `degraded: true` when the verdict was computed with an input it could not read. Freshness is explicit as `scoredAt` + `cacheExpiresAt`, the same pair the passport publishes — a cached value is up to five minutes old and says so
- `GET /api/health` — service status

Product spec §7.3 / §9.1 (2026-09-02) — object ids and measurement records, no key, per-IP limits stated on each:

- `GET /api/v1/resolve?q=<url|domain|address|tx|payee_id>` — reverse lookup: whatever you hold in, the canonical Resource / Endpoint / Payee / Settlement ids out. `resource_id` = sha256(method + " " + canonical_url). Returns identifiers only, never a recommendation. 60/min
- `GET /api/v1/resources/{resourceId}` — one Resource (sha256 hex) with its payees and links to `/decision`, `/facts` and the observatory page. 120/min
- `GET /api/v1/endpoints/{endpointId}` — one Endpoint by `endpoint_id` (sha256 of origin + path prefix) or its observatory uuid. 120/min
- `GET /api/v1/endpoints/{endpointId}/payees` — every `payee_id` (chain:address) declared under that endpoint. 120/min
- `GET /api/v1/payees/{address}/endpoints` — every endpoint that declares that payee as payTo; a bare 0x address is read as Base, a bare base58 address as Solana. 120/min
- `GET /api/v1/observatory/endpoints/{id}/facts` — the L0–L2 seller facts for one endpoint (liveness, settle-through with `n_probe_error` disclosed separately, conformance, availability, offer stability, 30-day settlements raw / real / test). Contains no score and no recommendation by design. 120/min
- `GET /api/v1/census/summary?chain=&window=7d|30d` — settlement census: `settlements_raw` and `settlements_real` (wash / test excluded) always together, never merged, with attribution and source breakdowns and the definition text in the body. 60/min, cached up to 20 minutes (see Freshness)
- `GET /api/v1/observatory/corrections?endpoint=&reason=&limit=&cursor=` — the correction log as JSON: every published verdict that later changed (`dispute_remeasure`, `settlement_backfill`, `reverify`, `path_template`) with `before` / `after`. No code path deletes or edits its rows, and since 2026-09-29 a ledger status change and its correction row are written in one database statement; the table is not write-protected against vet402 itself. Every row can be read (since 2026-09-29): at most 500 rows a page, `page.nextCursor` passed back as `cursor` returns the next older page (null on the last page), and `total` counts the rows matching `endpoint` and `reason` whatever the cursor — `?reason=settlement_backfill` gives the "Ledger status changes" count on /corrections. For a `purchase` row, `subject_id` is the `purchase_id` column of the ledger export. `settlement_path` names the path a `settlement_backfill` row took, worked out from `before` / `after` when the row is read: `verified_settled`, `claim_refuted`, `seller_named_tx_promoted` (the seller named the transaction in its payment response though its receipt did not say success — the export keeps `settlement_source=seller_claim` for it), `vet402_index_link`, `late_link_withdrawn`, `seller_named_tx_declined`, `other`. 60/min

Verification proves control of a wallet or an agent identity by signature. It is not an endorsement, and the score is computed independently of it.

## API — API key required

Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The decision route below also answers without a key (10/min per IP), and `/api/v1/resolve` needs none. Quotas and burst limits: https://vet402.com/docs/api#rate-limits

- `GET /api/v1/resources/{resourceId}/decision?role=payer|payee&payer=&caller_dialect=v1|v2&allow_without_l1=` — product spec §8.3 / §9.1, the canonical integration since 2026-09-02: the pre-payment (`role=payer`) or pre-service (`role=payee`, requires `payer`) decision. `facts` (SellerFacts or BuyerFacts) and `recommendation` (ALLOW / WARN / BLOCK) travel in the same document with `reason_codes`, `freshness`, `evidence` and `rules_version`; the transitional `score` is left out unless you pass `include_score=1`, and then carries `superseded_by: "recommendation"`; it is not the basis of the recommendation. Every reason code, with its meaning, what it means for the payer and whether the seller can fix it: https://vet402.com/docs/api#reason-codes (the same list is `DecisionReasonCode` in the OpenAPI file). Rules 2026-09-29.3 (`rules_version`): an L1 BLOCK needs money to have moved. A payment that settled on-chain (or a settle_failed row whose tx was verified) with no non-empty 2xx back is `l1_paid_not_delivered`: after the last delivery in the 30-day window, once is WARN and twice or more is BLOCK. A failed attempt where no money moved counts when `/sellers` puts it on the seller's side (the same failure on two different UTC days), and then it is a WARN at most (`l1_never_delivered` is a WARN); the others are left out with `l1_not_counted_unproven` (vet402 cannot show the failure was not its own; not sorted on `/sellers`) or `l1_not_counted_unconfirmed` (seen on one day so far). A paid attempt that got an empty 2xx with no settlement linked yet (no receipt, or a transfer awaiting on-chain verification) is not counted as a failure, but after the last delivery it adds `l1_empty_2xx_settlement_unknown` and is a WARN, never an ALLOW, until it settles; once a settlement is linked it counts as `l1_paid_not_delivered`. Attempts are also left out when the row shows vet402's side of the fault, when held for our own request shape or awaiting on-chain verification, and when the seller took no payment (when nothing was delivered, the reason code `l1_not_counted_held` names the second group and counts both kinds together: held (vet402's hold, a row with a `held_reason` in the ledger export) and awaiting on-chain verification (`settle_claimed`, whose `held_reason` is empty)). `l2_mismatch` is a BLOCK when the L2 evidence row names missing keys (`mismatch_kind: missing_keys`); with none on record it adds `l2_mismatch_unexplained` and is a WARN. A body vet402 could not read to the end is not a mismatch: since 2026-09-29 vet402 reads up to 256 KiB of a paid body and records a longer or unclosed JSON body as not checked (older rows cut at 16,000 bytes are read again the same way). `l1_latest_failed` (something delivered, but the latest counted attempt did not) is WARN. ALLOW needs a delivery within 30 days (the re-buy interval for a seller that has already delivered); otherwise WARN with `l1_stale`, also the word when every signed attempt is older than the 30-day window (`l1_not_attempted` means none was ever signed). `l1_basis` carries the counts (`n_not_counted` equals `n_attempts` exactly when the code is `l1_inconclusive`) and the last attempt, signed attempt and delivery with days since each. `verified_terms` (since 2026-09-29, role=payer) carries the terms vet402 actually paid on the last purchase whose delivery it confirmed — `pay_to`, `asset`, `amount` (base units, 6 decimals), `network`, `scheme`, `protocol`, `verified_at` — or null when nothing was ever delivered, and null on XRPL until the issuer is recorded (a currency code alone cannot tell RLUSD from a look-alike). 0x addresses are lowercase. Before you pay, compare it with the 402 you received: if the 402's payTo, asset, network or scheme differ, or its amount is higher, do not pay. An ALLOW is the fact that these terms delivered, not a guarantee for a different recipient or a higher price. L0 follows the published two-fail rule: one failed probe is WARN (`l0_unverified_single_fail`) when the listing is active, the probe before it passed and the failed probe is at most 120 hours old, otherwise BLOCK with `l0_unverified_single_fail_unconfirmed`; two consecutive fails are `l0_fail` and BLOCK. Limit of the method: vet402 buys with a fixed, published User-Agent, so a seller could answer vet402 differently from other buyers; other buyers' settlements show that they paid, not that they received, so the decision cannot detect this. Send `Idempotency-Key` to retry without spending a second rate-limit unit. Key-less at 10/min per IP since 2026-09-07 (same body; 429 `rate_limited` when spent). Your own policy (role=payer, since 2026-09-07): add `amount_usd`, `max_per_tx_usd` (default 1), `min_l1_deliveries` and/or `require_vet402_allow` (default true — a WARN refuses with `payee_recommendation_not_allow`, as the SDK's default does; `false` waives the WARN and needs `min_l1_deliveries` ≥ 1, else 400 `invalid_policy`) and the same document gains `caller_policy` — your rule applied server-side in the SDK's own words (`verdict` ALLOW | REFUSE, `reason_codes` `price_above_ceiling` / `evidence_unavailable` / `payee_recommendation_block` / `payee_recommendation_not_allow` / `insufficient_delivery_evidence`, `not_evaluated` naming what the server did not check, always `min_subgraph_receipts`). It never rewrites `recommendation`; without those queries the body is unchanged

The older score endpoints below need the same key. They return the transitional 0–100 score described at the top of this file (deprecated; the decision document above is the current integration) and the operational calls around it. Since 2026-09-29 each score response says so itself: `deprecated: true`, a `deprecation` object naming the decision endpoint to use instead, and the `Deprecation` / `Link` headers. The score's value is unchanged, and it rates a wallet or agent as a whole, so it can read ALLOW where the decision for one endpoint paid to that wallet reads WARN or BLOCK; decide with the decision endpoint:

- `GET /api/v1/payees/{address}/score` — the buyer-side question: should this payee be paid?
- `GET /api/v1/wallets/{address}/score` — trust score by wallet address (the path x402 middleware uses)
- `GET /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/score` — trust score by ERC-8004 agent ID (optional `?wallet=` verifies the registered wallet; optional `?chain=` selects an enabled chain, default Base)
- `POST /api/v1/scores/batch` — score up to 25 agents in one request
- `GET /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/history` — score history snapshots (paid plans)
- `POST /api/v1/payments/x402` — attest an x402 payment settlement after verification (idempotent on txHash)
- `POST /api/v1/events/{trustEventId}/outcome` — report what actually happened after a verdict; this is what the public accuracy ledger is computed from
- `GET|POST /api/v1/watchlist`, `DELETE /api/v1/watchlist/{id}` — watch an agent or wallet; verdict changes arrive as a `watch.verdict_changed` webhook
- `GET|POST /api/v1/webhooks`, `DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/{id}` — webhook subscriptions

## Open data — no key, and quotable

Three endpoints need no authentication and are published under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/): reuse, redistribute, chart or republish them, commercially or not, provided the source is named. The code is MIT; the data licence is separate and is in LICENSE-DATA in the repository.

- `GET /api/v1/observatory/state` — the aggregate snapshot. Carries `license`, `licenseUrl`, `retrievedAt` and `cite` in the body. Top-level totals include testnets; `byChain` is mainnet-only (`byChainScope`), so `sum(byChain)` can be below `totalEndpoints`. `publishedPass` counts endpoints on record whose latest L0 probe passed, including endpoints no longer listed, so it can exceed `activeEndpoints`; `publishedPassActive` is the part still listed, and `publishedPassActiveProbeOlderThan7d` the part of that last probed more than 7 days ago. `l1.endpointsSettled` (endpoints with a settled row, listed or not) is `l1.endpointsSettledSellerReceipt` (at least one transaction the seller named in its receipt) plus `l1.endpointsSettledIndexOnly` (every settled transaction found by vet402's own settlements index; no seller receipt).
- `GET /api/v1/observatory/history` — the daily series per chain.
- `GET /api/v1/observatory/export.csv?days=90` — the L1 purchase ledger, one row per paid attempt with its tx hash. Columns are only ever appended. `held_reason` says why a row is held (vet402's hold) rather than counted against the seller; it is empty on a row awaiting on-chain verification (`settle_claimed`), which is a different state (counted as `l1.awaitingReread` on `/api/v1/observatory/state`, not in `l1.inconclusive`). `request_body` says what the paid request carried: `declared` (the body the seller's own 402 declares, since 2026-09-17), `empty` (`{}`) or `none` (no body, recorded since 2026-09-20); blank means no record, not `empty`. `request_body_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the bytes sent on `declared` rows since 2026-09-20; the body itself is not republished. `settlement_source` says who named the transaction: `seller_claim` (the seller's settlement receipt) or `vet402_index` (no receipt came back and vet402's own settlements index found the transfer). `request_query` says which URL the paid request went to: `declared` (the query arguments the seller's own 402 declares, appended to the listed URL as declared; recorded on the row since 2026-09-20 and published as a column since 2026-09-21, on the networks in vet402's per-network allow-list), `empty` (the seller declared none) or `refused` (a declaration was there and vet402's rules did not use it). A declared name the listed URL already carries is dropped on its own and the other pairs are still appended, so a collision yields `refused` only when nothing is left to append. Blank means no record — a network the allow-list does not name, a Tempo row, a row that ended before a paid request, or a row before 2026-09-20 — and the column alone does not separate those. `request_query_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the appended pairs as one form-urlencoded string on `declared` rows; the query string itself is not republished, and the hash is for matching rather than a way of hiding it — the names and values are the seller's own and the 402 that answered the unpaid request is where they were read from. `spent_units` is the amount vet402 signed for on the attempt (what it put at stake), not an amount shown to have moved: a `settle_failed` row with no transaction still carries the price there. `confirmed_units` (since 2026-09-29) is the amount vet402 re-read on-chain as transferred: `spent_units` on `settled` rows and `0` on every other row, including `settle_claimed` rows still awaiting the re-read; `0` means no confirmed transfer, not a transfer shown not to have happened. `purchase_id` (since 2026-09-29) is the purchase's id, the `subject_id` of its rows in `/api/v1/observatory/corrections`. `scripts/declared-body-before-after.mjs` in the repository recomputes the before/after 2xx rate of the declared body from this CSV alone. Licence, retrieval time, row count and window are in the `x-vet402-*` and `Link` response headers, because a CSV has nowhere to put a comment.
- `GET /api/v1/observatory/l0/export.csv` — the latest public L0 verdict per endpoint (since 2026-09-29): one row per endpoint on record, listed or not, excluding endpoints paying vet402's own addresses — the data behind the L0 counts of `/api/v1/observatory/state`. Columns: `endpoint_id`, `resource_key`, `network`, `chain`, `network_class` (`mainnet` | `testnet` | `unclassified`), `listed`, `published_verdict` (`pass` | `fail` | `unverified`), `latest_probe_verdict`, `last_probed_at`, `latest_probe_older_than_7d`. Counting `published_verdict=pass` gives `publishedPass`; `network_class=mainnet` rows grouped by `chain` give `byChain`. 6/min, cached up to 45 minutes (see Freshness); definitions in `x-vet402-column-notes`, retrieval time in `x-vet402-retrieved-at`
- `GET /api/v1/sellers/export.csv` — the /sellers classification (since 2026-09-29): one row per active Base listing, classified by its latest purchase row with the same function /sellers uses, so counting rows by `outcome` (`delivered` | `pending` | `seller` | `vet402` | `unsorted` | `not_bought` | `not_tried`) gives the page's totals. Also `fix_mode`, `side_label`, `confirmed_seller`, `held_reason`, the latest row's time, status, network, HTTP status and `purchase_id`, and `in_ledger_export`. Served noindex, like the page, while its attribution is under review. 6/min, cached up to 45 minutes (see Freshness)

Cite as: KIZUNA Creation. vet402 observatory. Dataset, retrieved YYYY-MM-DD. https://vet402.com/api/v1/observatory/state — the retrieval date is not optional; every one of these numbers moves. Method, denominators and what each status means: https://vet402.com/observatory/methodology

Every response that carries a score or a published rate carries a `disclaimer` string in the payload, so the caveat travels with the number rather than living only on the web page.

Full machine-readable schema (OpenAPI 3.1, covering every public endpoint listed above, key-less and keyed, with `https://vet402.com` as the only production server): https://vet402.com/openapi.yaml — the same file is in the repository at https://github.com/kzmttkc/vet402/blob/main/docs/openapi.yaml, but cite the served URL.

## Packages

On npm, all from the same repository: `@vet402/sdk` (spend guard), `@vet402/middleware` (x402 request gate), `@vet402/mcp-server` (MCP tool). The SDK and the middleware both default to fail-closed — only an ALLOW passes, and a WARN, a BLOCK, a degraded verdict, or a partially measured one is denied unless the caller explicitly opts out.

## Implemented and live

- Address control verified: prove control of a wallet by signature, get a public page and an SVG badge
- Drop-in x402 middleware, REST API, and MCP tool
- Public accuracy ledger, published whether or not the numbers flatter us
- The x402 Observatory: L0 liveness probes across the full public discovery catalog, multi-chain (see /observatory/state for the breakdown), with delisting alerts for claimed sellers; L1 settle-through — real USDC purchases on the chains whose payer lane is switched on (the chains reached so far, with their counts, are the `l1.byChain` rows of https://vet402.com/api/v1/observatory/state), budget-capped, one purchase per endpoint per sweep window, recording every settlement and every refusal; L2 — a minimal structural check of the response against the seller's own declared schema

## Being built (not measurements yet)

- Writing verification records to the ERC-8004 Validation Registry. Not done yet because the registry is written in one direction: an agent's owner names a validator and opens the request, and the validator answers it. A validator cannot open a request about someone else's agent (`validationRequest` reverts with `Not authorized`, which is what vet402's fourteen attempts between 2026-08-21 and 2026-09-03 did). vet402 can answer the first request the day an agent owner sends one; none has named vet402 so far. The same account is §6 of https://vet402.com/#status

## Use cases

- x402 API providers deciding whether to accept a payment from an unfamiliar agent wallet
- Spending agents checking a counterparty before initiating a machine-to-machine payment
- Payees and agents publishing a signature-proven claim plus a badge, so counterparties can check them
- Marketplaces wanting a reputation signal without building their own scoring pipeline

## Chain

Base (ERC-8004 agent identity / reputation) is the default and the chain the scoring API measures on. The agent-score endpoint accepts `?chain=` to select another enabled chain; an unknown or disabled chain is a 400 with the live list, never a silent fallback to a different chain.

The observatory is a separate system and is not Base-only: L0 probing runs across every chain present in the public x402 discovery catalog, and https://vet402.com/observatory/state reports the current per-chain breakdown. L1 purchases run on the chains whose payer lane is switched on; the chains they have actually reached, with their counts, are the `l1.byChain` rows of https://vet402.com/api/v1/observatory/state, and that list is the one to read rather than any list written out here. Settlement is re-read on-chain with a chain-specific binding back to the signature vet402 holds: on Base and Arc the EIP-3009 authorization nonce, on Solana a memo vet402 wrote itself, on Tempo the indexed memo of a TIP-20 `TransferWithMemo`, on XRPL the hash of the signed blob. A purchase on a chain with no re-reader stays at `settle_claimed`; it is never silently paid on a substitute chain.

## Note on domain

The production URL is `vet402.com`, and it is the only canonical one. `agent-trust-tawny.vercel.app` is our own former deployment URL: it now issues a permanent (308) redirect to `vet402.com` and should not be cited, indexed, or linked as a source. `agent-trust.vercel.app` is a different thing again — an unrelated third-party service, not affiliated with vet402.

## Corrections

If a published score or verification result about a wallet you control is wrong, there is a free, key-less correction route open to anyone, customer or not — see section 8 of https://vet402.com/legal/terms#corrections

Corrections that are issued are published at https://vet402.com/corrections, and as JSON at https://vet402.com/api/v1/observatory/corrections. Read the count from there rather than from this file: it is not zero (the first corrections were published on 2026-09-04), and a number written here goes stale the next time we correct something.

## Citation

- You may cite the content on this site (front page, API docs, FAQ, accuracy ledger, blog) as long as you credit the source with the corresponding vet402.com URL.
- The same statement is published for human readers in section 4 of https://vet402.com/accuracy — this file is not the only place it exists.
- Figures on the accuracy ledger are rolling 90-day aggregates; cite them with the retrieval date, or quote the `generatedAt` timestamp from `GET /api/v1/accuracy`.
- Content current as of 2026-09-29. The measurements it points at are not: read them from the endpoints above, with the schedule in Freshness.

## Freshness

Every number on this site moves, so it is published with the schedule that moves it rather than as a timeless fact.

- Catalog sync (what is listed, what was delisted): daily, 01:00 UTC.
- L0 probes and the daily metrics rollup: daily, 10:30 UTC.
- L1 purchases: several runs a day. The scheduled run is 12:00 UTC; the operator adds runs at 00:00, 06:00 and 18:00 UTC, and, until 2026-10-05, further runs at 03:30, 09:30, 15:30 and 21:30 UTC. Read the time of each attempt from the ledger (`/api/v1/observatory/export.csv`) rather than from this list. On-chain settlement re-read: daily, 14:00 UTC. Most `settle_claimed` rows move to `settled` (or `settle_claim_refuted`) at the first re-read after the attempt, but a row stays at `settle_claimed` while the chain read cannot settle it either way, so some rows wait far longer than a day. Read the current count, the counts older than 1 and 7 days and the oldest attempt from `l1.awaitingReread`, `l1.awaitingRereadOlderThan1d`, `l1.awaitingRereadOlderThan7d` and `l1.awaitingRereadOldestAttemptAt` on `/api/v1/observatory/state` rather than assuming a day.
- Caches: the longest a copy you receive can lag the database, per surface. A shared-cache copy is served fresh for `s-maxage` and, with `stale-while-revalidate`, for that much longer while a fresh one is computed, so the most it can lag is the sum of the two. The `Age` response header says how long the copy you received sat in the cache. A page and the JSON can therefore show different numbers for a while after a run — compare their retrieval times rather than assume either is newer.
  - HTML pages that print observatory or /sellers aggregates (/, /observatory, /observatory/state, /sellers): rendered on every request, reading the aggregates through a 5-minute data cache (`PUBLIC_READ_REVALIDATE`, 300 s). A read after the window is served the older copy once while the fresh one is computed, so after a quiet spell one page view can be older than 5 minutes.
  - `GET /api/v1/resources/{resourceId}/decision`: no `Cache-Control`; each server instance reuses a decision it computed for up to 5 minutes (`DECISION_CACHE_TTL_MS`), so a copy can be up to 5 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/observatory/state`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=900, stale-while-revalidate=1800` — a copy can be up to 45 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/observatory/decisions`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=900, stale-while-revalidate=1800` — a copy can be up to 45 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/observatory/l0/export.csv`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=900, stale-while-revalidate=1800` — a copy can be up to 45 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/sellers/export.csv`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=900, stale-while-revalidate=1800` — a copy can be up to 45 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/accuracy`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=600, stale-while-revalidate=1200` — a copy can be up to 30 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/observatory/endpoints/{id}/purchases`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=600, stale-while-revalidate=1200` — a copy can be up to 30 minutes old.
  - `GET /api/v1/observatory/export.csv`, `/history`, `/anchors`, `/backtest`, `/concentration`: `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=7200` — a copy can be up to 3 hours old.
  - `GET /api/v1/census/summary`: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=900` — a copy can be up to 20 minutes old.
  - key-less object reads (`/api/v1/resolve`, `/resources/{id}`, `/endpoints/{id}`, `/endpoints/{id}/payees`, `/payees/{address}/endpoints`, `/observatory/endpoints/{id}/facts`, `/observatory/corrections`): `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300` — a copy can be up to 6 minutes old.
  - `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt`: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600` — a copy can be up to 1 hour old.
- `retrievedAt` in the JSON (`generatedAt` on `/api/v1/accuracy`, the `x-vet402-retrieved-at` header on the CSV) is the time vet402 read the numbers from its database, not the time you asked. It travels inside the cached copy, so it stays true whichever copy you were served, and it is the date to cite.

A measurement quoted without its retrieval date is not a measurement. Take the date from `retrievedAt` in the JSON, from the `x-vet402-retrieved-at` header on the CSV, or from the day you fetched the page.
